metadata.name: Ecodesign for Nim
metadata.description: Ecodesign rules for Nim code: bounded compile-time work, no needless sequence copies, deterministic cleanup.

perf.name: Nim — memory and build
perf.description: Keep copies and generated code under control (RGESN Algorithms/Architecture).

rules.title: Sequence copied instead of borrowed
rules.description: Assigning a seq copies it. Passing one by value into a proc copies it again. On a large sequence in a loop those copies dominate the work the proc actually does.
rules.recommendation: Take openArray[T] or a var/lent parameter so the caller's memory is used in place, and reserve with newSeqOfCap when the size is known.
rules.note: One openArray or lent parameter anywhere in the file silences the rule. Passing a small seq by value costs nothing measurable, so the size and the call frequency decide.

rules.title: Resource closed only on the happy path
rules.description: A file or socket closed at the end of a proc is never closed when an exception leaves early, which is exactly when the system is already struggling.
rules.recommendation: Wrap the acquisition in a defer or a try/finally so the close runs on every exit path.
rules.note: One defer or finally anywhere in the file silences the rule, even when another resource goes unclosed. Count the acquisitions against the releases before concluding.

rules.title: Unbounded compile-time generation
rules.description: Macros and static blocks run at build time and can generate more code than anyone reads. The build slows for everyone, and the binary carries the result to every deployment.
rules.recommendation: Keep generated code bounded and inspect it when it affects build time or binary size. A template is often enough where a macro was reached for.
